blocks.text: ORI:000–022 DETAILED REVIEW AND DELEGATED APPROVAL — CANONICAL

The Origin condition block was reconsidered from first principles under the standing delegated authority. The review compared five genuinely different architectures per root, scored 45 candidates across 360 criterion values, routed 115 English concepts without forced atomization, passed all 18 canonical packet checks, passed all 19 focused Origin condition-layer soundness checks, and passed the complete authority regression. All deterministic generated forms remained unchanged.

Approved architecture: ORI:0xx names substrate-neutral ontological conditions. The inward triplet qualifies source-grounding; the outward triplet qualifies one distinct referent’s existence in the relevant reality; and the systemic triplet qualifies a shared-world condition. The third trit changes only persistent, occurrent or operative, or latent status. Lexical latency means membership without present expression, not uncertainty, possibility, counterfactuality, concealment, planning, scheduling, or future time.

ORI:000 — persistent source-ground condition — A persistent ontological condition by which one referent is grounded as a source from which another state of affairs may originate, independently of whether that grounding is presently operative.

ORI:001 — operative source-ground condition — An ontological condition by which one referent is grounded as a source from which another state of affairs may originate and that grounding is presently operative.

ORI:002 — latent source-ground condition — An ontological condition by which one referent is grounded as a source from which another state of affairs may originate and that grounding exists without being presently operative.

ORI:010 — persistent distinct-existence condition — A persistent ontological condition under which one distinct referent obtains as part of the relevant reality, independently of whether it is presently manifesting or changing.
ORI:011 — occurrent distinct-existence condition — An ontological condition under which one distinct referent is presently manifesting or changing as part of the relevant reality.
ORI:012 — latent distinct-existence condition — An ontological condition under which one distinct referent belongs to the relevant reality without presently manifesting or changing within it.

ORI:020 — persistent shared-world condition — A persistent ontological condition that jointly constrains what obtains across one shared reality, independently of whether that condition is presently being expressed through change.
ORI:021 — occurrent shared-world condition — An ontological condition that is presently being expressed through change across one shared reality.
ORI:022 — latent shared-world condition — An ontological condition that belongs to one shared reality without presently being expressed through change across it.

Design boundary: these roots do not silently encode a causal link, temporal beginning, observation, representation, proposition, physical substrate, productive history, authorship, provenance, or modal force. Persistent status may co-occur with occurrence or latency; occurrence and latency are mutually exclusive for the same condition at one reference time. Runtime [2]/num remains assertion-level uncertainty and never selects lexical latency.
